Subject: Initial questions: addendum classification, telemetry sampling & export controls

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. Aegis is finalizing the US state privacy addendum and we have a few items we need clarified from Redwood before we can proceed:

- Processor vs Service Provider: our legal team expects a clear statement that Redwood will act as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and applicable state laws. Can you confirm the exact clause you propose?
- Telemetry sampling: we collect limited telemetry from API integrations. Will sampled telemetry aggregated for performance stats be considered "sale" or "share" under your handling? We need commitments on sampling rates and whether telemetry is treated as deidentified.
- Export controls & cross-border data export: any exports to non-US regions for model tuning or cache warm-up? If so, what controls and contract language can you provide?
- Subprocessor roster and notice timing: please send the current roster and confirm your notice window for onboarding emergency subprocessors.
- Retention windows: we need concrete retention commitments for request logs, KV caches (prefix caching), and telemetry and how deletion requests will be applied to cached tokens.

Attached is our RFI (Aegis_RFI_CC_Addendum.docx) with redlines and reference clauses. Can we have a short call to walk these items and agree on language? Ideally this week.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Park
Director, Vendor Risk & Privacy
AegisHealth

Subject: Re: Initial questions: addendum classification, telemetry sampling & export controls

Hi Sam — appreciated the clear list. Quick answers and proposed next steps below; happy to jump on a 30-minute call to align.

1) Classification: Redwood proposes to accept the role of "service provider" (operator) for the production inference API for standard usage patterns. We will accept contractual language that maps to the CCPA/CPRA "service provider" definition and will not sell customer data. I'll attach a redline of the addendum with the clause inserted.

2) Telemetry sampling: sampled performance telemetry (latency, error rates, aggregate token counts) will be treated as operational metrics and processed in aggregated/deidentified form. We propose a maximum sampling window (1% of requests by default, configurable on dedicated/private deployments) and an option for customers to opt-out of telemetry sharing on Dedicated/Private. We'll provide a telemetry sampling guide and a commitment that telemetry will not be used to derive PII or sold.

3) Export controls / cross-border: For Hosted, some maintenance tasks and diagnostic jobs may route small diagnostic payloads to engineering teams in our EU/US regions for troubleshooting. We can commit to: a) excluding raw customer prompt/response payloads from diagnostic exports (only hashes/triaged snippets with explicit consent), b) offering onshore fallback for export-sensitive customers (Dedicated/Private), and c) an export-control clause stating we won't route customer content to jurisdictions restricted by agreement without prior notice.

4) Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor roster and our standard 30-day notice window for non-emergency subprocessors. For emergency security subprocessors (e.g., DDoS mitigation), we have a documented emergency onboarding process and will notify customers within 72 hours with a remediation plan.

5) Retention: proposed retention windows are below — we can include them in the addendum as concrete numbers: request logs (60 days default, encrypted at rest), KV/cache traces (48 hours, unless pinned by customer for performance), telemetry aggregates (13 months for trend analysis), and audit logs (13 months). Deletion requests will remove customer-identifiable content from persistent logs within 30 days; cached KV tokens will be pruned at next eviction cycle if they cannot be deterministically deleted.

Next steps:
- I'm attaching a redline (us-privacy-addendum-redline.pdf) that incorporates the above language.
- Proposed 30-minute sync: Thu 2027-03-11 at 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm.

I can also loop in Aditya for the telemetry sampling thresholds and Marissa for escalation/legal sign-off.

Best,
Irene Choi
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.example.com
[Attachment: us-privacy-addendum-redline.pdf (pdf)]

Looping in recommended thresholds and operational notes for telemetry sampling. Quick bullets:

- Default sampling: 1% of requests across the hosted fleet for aggregated metrics is typical; we can offer 0.1% for sensitive accounts on hosted if they opt in for stricter privacy. Dedicated/Private deployments: sampling disabled by default.
- Aggregate deidentification: samples are stripped of prompt/response PII server-side before any analytics pipeline. We store hashes for dedup and troubleshooting.
- KV/cache retention: cache TTL default 48 hours; we provide a control flag to allow customers to set TTL to 0 (no caching) for privacy-sensitive datasets.
- Export/diagnostic pipeline: we can provide a toggle for customers to restrict any cross-region diagnostic exports; default is on but we will enforce no raw prompt dumps.

I've attached the telemetry-sampling-guidance.xlsx with a matrix of sampling rates vs. expected signal-to-noise and cost impact. If Legal wants hard canned language for the addendum about sampling caps, propose: "Redwood will not sample more than 1% of Customer requests for operational telemetry without Customer consent, except in emergency incident investigations."

Aditya
Sr. Product Engineer, Runtime
[Attachment: telemetry-sampling-guidance.xlsx (xlsx)]
